unfold.unfolded: Let $S$ be an ordered semigroup and $m\ge 1$ an integer. $S$ is $m$-bi-interior-simple if $S$ has no $m$-bi-interior ideals other than $S$ itself, that is, every $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$ equals $S$. Here a non-empty subset $B$ of $S$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$ if $(BS^mB]\cap(S^mBS^m]\subseteq B$ and $(B]=B$, where $(X]=\{x\in S : x\le y \text{ for some } y\in X\}$ and $S^m$ is the set of all products of $m$ elements of $S$.
notes: The context defines the m-bi-interior ideal of Definition 2.1, inlined here; the range of m is taken as positive as in the other definitions, which the original does not state.
The phrase other than S itself is read as: every m-bi-interior ideal equals S.
The empty set is not an m-bi-interior ideal, since the definition requires a non-empty subset.
